question_text: This is Captain Joel Randolph, the commanding officer of the Federation starship USS Yorktown in Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home (1986). His character appears on a screen at Starfleet Command to report that his ship is losing power to an alien probe, which serves to establish the dire, high-stakes threat in the opening sequence of the movie. The actor who played Captain Randolph is the first ever person to have appeared in both the James Bond and Star Trek movie franchises. In fact, after this role, Star Trek fans joked that he actually beat the Borg in real life. Id the actor (10 pts).
answer_text: Vijay Amritraj. He played Captain Joel Randolph in Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home, and also appeared as Sadruddin in the James Bond film Octopussy opposite Roger Moore.

question_text: The book X has a deep, rather weird connection with George W Bush. During the early days of his presidency, Bush was rarely seen without the book as he famously read it across the country. In fact, several artworks from the book remain in the collection of the George W. Bush Presidential Library and Museum in Texas. Commentators have mocked his connection with the book, referencing his time as the Texas governor, saying that just like the protagonist of the book, he ate his way through Texas oil wells, baseball teams, and the state as a whole, before spinning a political _____ and emerging as president. Which hugely popular book, which features a biological mistake (the protagonist emerges from a _____ instead of a scientifically accurate chrysalis), was Bush seemingly obsessed with? (10 pts)
answer_text: The Very Hungry Caterpillar, by Eric Carle.

question_text: In July 1956, 10-year old Richard Stokes got a gift from his dad - the tickets to watch something for the first time in his life. As luck would have it, Stokes and his dad witnessed an event that had never happened before in history. He would later recall that he was so young that he didn't remember the moment it happened, but remembered how the crowd erupted in absolute ecstasy. He eventually became a businessman who settled in Germany. On one of his business trips, this time to India, he decided to give himself a treat on his birthday by booking tickets to the ________. As luck would have it, he witnessed the exact same history-making event as the one he saw 43 years ago. Even more remarkably, it was only the second ever instance of it happening. What rarest of rare occurrences did Richard Stokes witness, not once but twice? (10 pts)
answer_text: 10 wickets in an innings, taken by a single bowler in a Test match. Jim Laker (England vs Australia, 1956) and Anil Kumble (India vs Pakistan, 1999).

question_text: The Maltese Falcon is a 1941 American film based on the eponymous Dashiell Hammett novel and was among the first movies in the film noir genre. It was the great John Huston's first film and starred Humphrey Bogart as Detective Sam Spade. One of the arch villains in the film was a 300-pound British man played by Sydney Greenstreet, after whom X was named. __ ___ __ was another novel from Hammett, which led to its own film series and again featured a detective as its protagonist. Y got its initial name from this novel, but the name was changed to what we know it as today, as its design had to be changed into something smaller upon testing. Eventually, Y was given a new name that sounded like the opposite of X. Id X and Y (5 pts each).
answer_text: X: Fat Man (the atomic bomb dropped on Nagasaki, named after Sydney Greenstreet's heavyset villain character Kasper Gutman in The Maltese Falcon). Y: Little Boy (the atomic bomb dropped on Hiroshima, which got its early name from Hammett's novel The Thin Man before being renamed to sound like the opposite of Fat Man).

question_text: Connect (10 pts). Four picture clues are shown: 1) A poster for The Barber of Seville, with the text: F is the clever, fast-talking titular barber and a master trickster. 2) An image of Jupiter with its four largest moons, with the text: The 4 moons of Jupiter, Ganymede, Callisto, Io, Europa are collectively named after G. 3) The cover of William Golding's novel Lord of the Flies, with the text: B, a powerful demon in Christian and Jewish traditions served as the inspiration for the title. 4) A drawing of a stock clown character carrying a guitar, with the text: S, the stock clown in 16th century Italian theatre who got his name from the Italian word for 'Skirmish'.
answer_text: Bohemian Rhapsody by Queen. The connection is the words Figaro, Galileo, Beelzebub, and Scaramouche, all of which appear in the song's lyrics.

question_text: The Royal Western India Turf Club established the Indian Derby, a fixture in Mumbai's horse racing circuit in 1943. The race is a Grade 1 event open to four-year-old Indian thoroughbreds. It is run over a distance of 2,400 metres on the turf track at the Mahalaxmi Race Course. The early 1966 racing season was historically significant for the RWITC due to multiple reasons - it was the only time the event was held on a Monday; a chestnut colt named Red Rufus became the first horse in history to win the Indian Triple Crown winning all three classic races; and in conjunction with the racing season, India hosted the Asian Racing Conference for the very first time in 1966. Curiously, a massive billboard was placed near the track, with the headline Thoroughbread. What's the funda? (10 pts)
answer_text: It was the first topical Amul Girl ad, playing on 'Thoroughbred' as 'Thoroughbread', referencing the Indian Derby and Red Rufus's Triple Crown win, with the tagline 'utterly butterly Amul'.

question_text: Where would you find these lessons? (10 pts). 1. Prospecting: Not every prospect or partner will be the right fit. Identifying the right fit takes time. 2. Discovery: Doing deep discovery is critical. 3. Demo: If you're confident there is a strong fit, showing your product to potential buyers is essential. 4. Pricing: After demoing and, ideally, getting their hands on the product, your prospect is ready to buy. 5. Negotiations: There will be concessions. One party may want something the other party isn't willing to give up. 6. Handling Objections: Even after pricing and negotiations, there may be some resistance. 7. Closing: If you've done your work in the earlier stages of the relationship, when it comes time to close the deal, you'll have nothing to worry about.
answer_text: In a LinkedIn post by Bryan Shankman, Owner at SuperSeller, titled 'I proposed to my girlfriend this weekend. Here's what it taught me about B2B sales,' which shows a photo of him proposing on a beach and then satirically maps the proposal onto the stages of a B2B sales process.

question_text: Signor Felice X was an Italian chemist and former soldier who patented a drink called 'Ferro-China X' - it was a liqueur made from the bark of cinchona, iron salts and a concoction of herbs, and was marketed as a hangover and health tonic. In the 1920s, the company saw the United States as its next big opportunity - though the country was going through Prohibition, medical health tonics with alcohol were legally allowed. To ramp up global production, the company needed a steady supply of exotic herbs and roots and looked to India. The plan never really took off and post-WW2, the operations went almost entirely dormant. After the war, the founder's grandson, Vittorio Cacceiandra, traveled to India to revive the business. What he saw in India though gave him the idea to pivot to a new category, to something that wasn't available in abundance in a young nation. They abandoned the old herb operations and built a brand-new factory in Thane to sell the product we know them for today. When it hit the market, Indians thought it was a joke, an indulgent luxury, and it duly flopped. Until, Y acquired it for a paltry sum of ₹4 lakh in 1969. Id X (6 pts) and Y (4 pts).
answer_text: X: Bisleri. Y: Parle. Felice Bisleri's family business, originally selling the tonic Ferro-China Bisleri, pivoted in India to bottled mineral water, which flopped until Parle acquired the Bisleri brand for ₹4 lakh in 1969.

question_text: X is one of the most iconic and gruelling obstacle courses in Y, with participants having to race from one end of the course to the other before time expires. There are 7 obstacle zones for contestants to tackle: 1. Conveyor zone, 2. Caterpillar zone, 3. Trampoline zone, 4. Revolving Comaneci zone, 5. Animal zone, 6. Monster zone, 7. Heaven and Hell zone. Id X (7 pts) and Y (3 pts)
answer_text: X: Gauntlet (the final obstacle course). Y: Takeshi's Castle (the Japanese game show).

question_text: The eruption of Mt Krakatoa, Indonesia, in 1883 was catastrophic - it produced the largest recorded sound in history, took over 36,000 lives, and had massive ripple effects globally. It lowered global average temperatures by about 1.2°C for several years and caused strikingly vivid, reddish sunsets worldwide. In 2004, Donald W. Olson, a physics and astronomy professor at Texas State University, and his colleagues Russell L. Doescher and Marilynn S. Olson theorised that the effects of the eruption were also behind X. After studying the creator Y's journals and investigating sky phenomena that might have influenced Y, Olson and his colleagues theorized it was the eruption of Krakatoa volcano that produced the colorful twilights. 'One of the high points of our research trip to Oslo came when we rounded a bend in the road and realized we were standing in the exact spot where Y had been 120 years ago,' Olson recalled. 'We could see that Y was looking to the southwest - exactly where the Krakatoa twilights appeared in the winter of 1883-84.' What were Olsson & Co. talking about? X (6 pts), Y (4 pts)
answer_text: The Scream by Edvard Munch. X is the painting's fiery, blood-red sky, and Y is Edvard Munch, the painter, whose vivid depiction of the sky is theorised to have been inspired by the colourful twilights caused by the Krakatoa eruption.

question_text: "Let's intertwine X-Y as fans will do for generations to come. It's.....HUMANS TIRE (but not _____)" wrote Sports Illustrated senior writer Jon Wertheim in his July 4 column in 2010. What insane wordplay, which he credited online fan forums to, is referenced here? Give funda. (10 pts)
answer_text: X and Y are John Isner and Nicolas Mahut, who played the longest match in tennis history at Wimbledon 2010 (6-4, 3-6, 6-7(7), 7-6(3), 70-68, lasting 11 hours 5 minutes over three days on Court No. 18). The wordplay is that 'HUMANS TIRE' is an anagram of 'ISNER MAHUT'.

question_text: X is one of PwC's longest standing American accounts, with the relationship lasting over 90 years. As with all major clients, they manage X's internal board elections, audit their financial statements, and prepare their taxes. Only a Senior Partner/Corporate Account Lead with 20-30+ years of experience, a licensed CPA designation, and specialisation in the __________ industry is handed the keys to the deepest secrets of X. Prior to 2017, only 14 such Senior Partners were ever exposed to these secrets. All of the Senior Partners have historically chosen a trusted Co-Leader, another highly experienced partner, as their wingmen for this secret exercise. Since the highly publicised fiasco in 2017, when one of the partners was apparently distracted by posting photos on Twitter, the protocol has been made stricter, with a third senior partner also in on the secret now. Needless to say, the culprits in 2017 were removed from the account and had to be assigned personal bodyguards in the aftermath of the faux pas. Which account, what fiasco? (10 pts)
answer_text: The account is the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences (the Oscars), for whom PwC tabulates and safeguards the award results. The fiasco was the 2017 Best Picture mix-up, when La La Land was mistakenly announced as the winner before it was corrected on stage that Moonlight had actually won, after a PwC partner was distracted posting photos on social media backstage.

question_text: Steve Matteson originally named his neo-grotesque creation "Bierstadt", after Mount Bierstadt, a 14,000-ft peak in the Rocky Mountains of his native Colorado. He felt the massive, sturdy look of the mountain matched his creation. However, his clients found an issue with the name - Bierstadt in German meant "Beer Town" and they were afraid the name wouldn't be taken seriously. To find a better name, Matteson looked back at his time living in California during the 1990s. He chose X, a small unincorporated beach town in Santa Cruz County where he loved to vacation. The town had diverse landscapes, shifting from beaches and ocean fog straight up into massive redwood forests, giving the name a sense of versatility. What is his creation that almost all of us would have noticed fairly recently? (10 pts)
answer_text: Aptos, the typeface that replaced Calibri as the default font in Microsoft 365, named after Aptos, California (other font weights/siblings in the family include Tenorite, Seaford, Grandview and Skeena).

question_text: An image shows Prakash Varma alongside another actor in a tense scene from the Malayalam film Thudarum. This is Prakash Varma, who plays the antagonist in the Mohanlal movie Thudarum (2025), which went on to become one of the highest grossers in the history of Malayalam cinema. It was his acting debut, and he received widespread acclaim for his performance. He has also spent decades behind the camera and some of his most popular works have achieved near universal popularity in India, peaking in the summer of 2009 with X, which he directed in just 10 days. The shoot was in Cape Town, with everything filmed in studio to maintain secrecy. To make the actors look small, the crew built giant backdrops with nondescript walls and floors. It was also shot at a higher frame rate, giving the protagonists the trademark movement we associate with them. Id X (10 pts).
answer_text: The Vodafone ZooZoo advertising campaign (2009), featuring the white, big-headed ZooZoo characters.

question_text: X was one of the most popular and profitable games at the time of release, spawning multiple sequels. The game's title came from the producer and designer, Randy Breen, reminiscing to his colleagues about driving along Y to meet his friends and thinking to himself "Man, if you wiped out here, you'd get some serious X". The original working title was therefore "X on Y", which was later shortened to just "X". Now Y wasn't any ordinary location either, lending its name to a movie voted by BBC and IndieWire as the "Best film of the 21st Century". The director of the movie lived close to Y and stated in an interview, "At night, you ride on the top of the world. In the daytime you ride on top of the world, too, but it's mysterious, and there's a hair of fear because it goes into remote areas. You feel the history of Hollywood in that road." Id X (5 pts), Y (5 pts).
answer_text: X: Road Rash (the motorcycle racing video game). Y: Mulholland Drive (the Los Angeles road, also the title of David Lynch's 2001 film, which was voted the best film of the 21st century in a BBC poll).

question_text: Hardas Laxmanrao Nagrale, popularly known as Babu Hardas, was a prominent labour leader and social reformer from Nagpur. He lived a brief life and died at 35 but is remembered to this day for organising beedi and mill workers and women workers in the Nagpur region. Today, thousands of activists and families gather to pay homage to him as a symbol of social justice every year - an event known as Babu Hardas Mela, that has been organised on the day after Makar Sankranti for the past 86 years on the banks of the Kanan river. Hardas was a strong opponent of superstitious customs, especially idol worship. Instead, he urged the public to revere those who made an actual difference in their lives and arranged annual community dinners on the death anniversary of Chokhamela, a 14th century Bhakti saint from Vidarbha who was considered one of the earliest __ ____ poets in India. In 1938, at a public gathering in Makranpur, Aurangabad, Hardas was slated to speak publicly to the members of the Samata Sainik Dal and started his speech with 'X', something he had coined. Id X (10 pts).
answer_text: Jai Bhim, the slogan coined by Babu Hardas, which was later adopted and popularised by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.

question_text: Tie Break. Why has Kinder Joy become Yoj Rednik in their new Funko collab? An image shows four Kinder Joy eggs from different collaborations (Super Mario, Jurassic World, DC), with the fourth egg's packaging appearing flipped so its text reads backwards/upside down, and a blanked-out teal rectangle covering part of its branding.
answer_text: Stranger Things - 'Upside Down'. The Kinder Joy x Funko Stranger Things packaging is printed flipped/mirrored to evoke the show's 'Upside Down' dimension, making the 'Kinder Joy' logo read backwards as 'Yoj Rednik'.

question_text: Tie Break. Connect these two flags (exhaustive). Images show the flag of Spain and the flag of Mexico.
answer_text: The only national flags with pink. Spain's flag has a pink/magenta element within its coat of arms, and Mexico's flag likewise features a touch of pink within its coat of arms - these two are said to be the only national flags containing the colour pink.
